summary: Since the auth-service release at 14:10 UTC, tokens are failing signature verification, and the api-gateway 401 rate rose from 0.2% to 30%. Web and mobile users are being logged out and cannot log back in, so a core access flow is broken for many customers.

hypotheses.title: Signing key or key configuration changed in the auth-service release
hypotheses.reasoning: The failures started right after the 14:10 UTC release, and the logs say 'token signature verification failed'. This points to tokens being signed with a different key, algorithm or key ID than the one used to verify them. That would invalidate existing sessions (the logouts) and could also break newly issued tokens (the failed re-logins).
next_steps: Compare the auth-service signing key, key ID and algorithm configuration between the previous and the new release, and check the deploy diff for secret or config changes.
Query ELK for auth-service logs from 14:10 UTC onward and check whether newly issued tokens fail verification immediately, or only tokens issued before the release.
Decode the header of a failing token (without logging its contents) and compare its kid/alg with the keys currently published or configured for verification.

hypotheses.title: Instance or key mismatch during rollout: only some auth-service instances run the new key or config
hypotheses.reasoning: A 30% 401 rate rather than near 100% suggests partial failure. A partially completed or inconsistent rollout, where some instances sign with one key and others verify with another, would explain this. It would also explain why some users can still authenticate.
next_steps: In ELK, group 'token signature verification failed' errors by auth-service instance or pod and by version to see whether failures are concentrated on specific instances.
Check the rollout status and confirm that all auth-service instances run the same release and load the same signing keys.
Check whether api-gateway has its own cached verification keys or JWKS, and whether its cache refresh time matches the 14:10 UTC release.

hypotheses.title: Regression in token issuance or validation code in the new release, unrelated to key configuration
hypotheses.reasoning: The release may have changed how tokens are built or validated (claims, encoding, serialization), so valid tokens fail the signature check even though the keys are unchanged. This differs from a key problem because the same keys would still be in use.
next_steps: Review the release changelog and diff for changes to token generation, serialization or validation libraries.
Roll back auth-service to the previous version in a staging or canary environment and check whether login and token verification succeed, which would confirm the release as the cause.
Compare the ELK error stack traces from auth-service before and after 14:10 UTC to find new exception types.
